rows.notes: The document is explicitly a narrative literature review (title 'Review'; Section 1 states its aims are to examine applications via 'a detailed literature analysis'; Data Availability: Not applicable). It reports no own data, experiment, survey or model runs. The >95% detection accuracy and 81<U+2013>95% outbreak prediction figures in the abstract and Section 8.1 are summaries of other studies, not the authors' own results; the 10<U+2013>16% yield-loss figure is cited from Oerke and Savary et al. as a general global loss estimate, not a measured reduction attributable to AI. No AI-based app or scheduling tool for pest control is tested by the authors.

Same document: a narrative review with no primary data. The claimed effect on crop production (reducing yield losses by 16%) is not an own result; the 10<U+2013>16% figure is a cited global estimate of annual crop losses to disease (refs 3,4), and the review only speculates that AI tools 'hold promise to boost yields'. No own evidence on app-based scheduling or any effect on yield.
